strategy.summary: Commit 72802a9 ("Show each line's product name on an order") added a third sequential store round trip (productNames) to GET /orders/:id, raising the `detail` scenario's p95 from 22 ms to 31 ms (+44.3%, 32 ms on rerun). Guard it with a scenario-tagged p95 threshold in perf/orders.js at the baseline plus 20% headroom (existing thresholds, checks and scenarios kept unchanged), record the defect and file it for a person to fix.
inScope: p95 latency threshold for the detail scenario in perf/orders.js
Defect record and GitHub issue for the detail slowdown
outOfScope: Changing application code to recover the time
detail p99 and search p95/p99: within baseline noise per the work item, not confirmed slowdowns
assumptions: Threshold derived from the baseline median p95 22 ms with the run's 20% headroom: p(95)<26.4
The app runs for real at BASE_URL (default http://localhost:4310); nothing is faked
run_tests runs k6 with --no-thresholds in smoke mode, so the counted run proves the script runs, not that the threshold passes; under real load it is expected to fail until the app is fast again
The existing script is only extended: its scenarios, checks and global thresholds stay as they are

risks.description: A threshold too tight given noise (baseline cv 5.2%, range 21–24 ms) could flake
risks.mitigation: 26.4 ms sits above the highest good run (24 ms) and well below the slow 31–32 ms

acceptanceCriteria.text: The detail scenario's p95 http_req_duration stays within 20% of the last good runs' baseline (22 ms), i.e. below 26.4 ms

testCases.title: detail scenario keeps p95 latency under 26.4 ms
steps: Run perf/orders.js under its constant-arrival-rate scenarios
testCases.expected: Threshold holds at the baseline level; currently fails (p95 ~31 ms) until the extra round trip is removed
testCases.rationale: Guards p95 latency of detail, which regressed +44.3% at 72802a9: GET /orders/:id now awaits productNames() as a third sequential store round trip (~6–9 ms each) after findOrder and orderLines, instead of fetching names with the lines in orderLines' single query as the commit message claims.

strategy.environmentNotes: k6 against the orders-api at BASE_URL (http://localhost:4310 by default).

defects.title: Order detail p95 latency up 44% since product names were added (extra store round trip)
defects.description: perf/orders.js › detail (GET /orders/:id): p95 latency 22 ms (median of 5 good runs, range 21–24 ms) → 31 ms (+44.3%), 32 ms on rerun. Bisect: first slow at 72802a9fba0d "Show each line's product name on an order". The diff adds `await productNames(...)` in src/app.js's order route after findOrder and orderLines; productNames (src/store.js) does its own roundTrip() (~6–9 ms). The request now makes 3 sequential store queries instead of 2. The commit message says the names come "in one query with the lines", but they're fetched in a separate query. Fix: return each line's product name from orderLines' existing query (it already joins products for priceCents), or run the lookup in parallel. The threshold 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}': p(95)<26.4 (baseline + 20%) guards it.
defects.evidence: k6 run perf/orders.js on 35eaba9: ✗ 'p(95)<26.4' p(95)=31.38ms for {scenario:detail}; "thresholds on metrics 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}' have been crossed", exit 99.

culprit.subject: Show each line's product name on an order
culprit.body: The order page listed product ids, which support had to look up. The names come from the store in one query with the lines.
